answer.text:
动态无功资源在指定电压带宽内随电网电压变化自动、实时连续调节无功输出，所依据的是NERC指南；其运行方式为维持设定点电压，或采用电压下垂模式。

findings.rationale: The cited NERC guideline directly contradicts the claim: dynamic reactive resources adjust output automatically in real-time over a continuous range in response to grid voltage changes; the fixed-output description applies to static, not dynamic, resources.

excerpts.text:
Background 
 
• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements: 
• Fixed Shunt Devices: fixed shunt reactive devices include shunt capacitors and reactors. These devices 
have a fixed nominal rating and their reactive power production or consumption is dependent on

applicability_conditions: NERC guideline applies to the North American bulk power system; voluntary, region-specific practices vary.

citation_reviews.rationale:

The answer claims dynamic resources have fixed output once connected, cannot continuously adjust with voltage, and use only a fixed voltage set-point; each of these reverses the source's meaning. • Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected.

excerpts.text:
Background 
 
• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements: 
• Fixed Shunt Devices: fixed shunt reactive devices include shunt capacitors and reactors. These devices 
have a fixed nominal rating and their reactive power production or consumption is dependent on

excerpts.text:
Background 
 
• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements: 
• Fixed Shunt Devices: fixed shunt reactive devices include shunt capacitors and reactors. These devices 
have a fixed nominal rating and their reactive power production or consumption is dependent on

applicability_conditions: North American bulk power system context; guideline is voluntary, not a Chinese standard.

actual_question: 按给定NERC资料解释静态无功资源的电压依赖；这些资料能否给出某匿名厂站所需补偿容量？

initial_answer.text: 按该资料，静态无功资源的能力随电压平方变化。给定资料没有该匿名厂站的网络模型、运行点与补偿目标，不能据此给出具体补偿容量。

answer.text:
按NERC资料，动态无功资源能在规定电压带宽内实时、连续、自动调节无功输出（可维持设定电压或电压下垂模式）；静态无功资源在额定电压下输出固定，能力随电压平方变化，按系统条件投切，接入后只提供固定标称无功。

这一区别不能单独保证某厂站故障后电压稳定：资料只说明N-1等扰动后的系统电压/稳定准则，需结合该厂站网络模型、运行点、电压限值与故障假设做研究。
missing_information: 匿名厂站的网络模型、运行点、电压限值及故障/N-1/-N-2假设与无功裕度研究

answer.text: 动态无功资源输出固定，静态无功资源能实时连续自动调节。因此只要选用静态无功资源，就能保证匿名厂站故障后电压稳定。

excerpts.text:
Background 
 
• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements: 
• Fixed Shunt Devices: fixed shunt reactive devices include shunt capacitors and reactors. These devices 
have a fixed nominal rating and their reactive power production or consumption is dependent on

Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

Background 
 
• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements: 
• Fixed Shunt Devices: fixed shunt reactive devices include shunt capacitors and reactors. These devices 
have a fixed nominal rating and their reactive power production or consumption is dependent on

Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

Background 
 
• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements: 
• Fixed Shunt Devices: fixed shunt reactive devices include shunt capacitors and reactors. These devices

excerpts.text:
Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

answer.text:
按NERC资料，动态无功资源能在规定电压带宽内实时、连续、自动调节无功输出（可维持设定电压或电压下垂模式）；静态无功资源在额定电压下输出固定，能力随电压平方变化，按系统条件投切，接入后只提供固定标称无功。

这一区别不能单独保证某厂站故障后电压稳定：资料只说明N-1等扰动后的系统电压/稳定准则，需结合该厂站网络模型、运行点、电压限值与故障假设做研究。

按NERC资料，动态无功资源在指定电压带宽内随电网电压变化实时连续自动调节无功输出，可维持设定电压或按电压下垂模式运行；静态无功资源在额定电压下输出固定，其能力随电压平方变化，按系统条件投切，投切可为手动或自动，但连通后仅提供固定的额定无功贡献。

Background 
 
• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements: 
• Fixed Shunt Devices: fixed shunt reactive devices include shunt capacitors and reactors. These devices 
have a fixed nominal rating and their reactive power production or consumption is dependent on

excerpts.text:
Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

applicability_conditions: NERC guideline applies to the North American bulk power system; recommendations voluntary, not a Chinese standard.
Guarantee would require plant-specific study; source only addresses contingency analysis expectations.

conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected.

Background 
 
• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements: 
• Fixed Shunt Devices: fixed shunt reactive devices include shunt capacitors and reactors. These devices

Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

answer.text:
按NERC资料，动态无功资源在指定电压带宽内随电网电压变化实时连续自动调节无功输出，可维持设定电压或按电压下垂模式运行；静态无功资源在额定电压下输出固定，其能力随电压平方变化，按系统条件投切，投切可为手动或自动，但连通后仅提供固定的额定无功贡献。

仅凭这一调节方式区别不能单独保证匿名厂站故障后电压稳定：该结论还需厂站网络模型、运行点、电压限值与故障/预想事故假设等专项研究，NERC资料只说明资源类型与N-1扰动后应维持在紧急电压限值内的分析框架，未证明任何特定厂站通过电压稳定研究，本次也未做仿真或安全认证。

Background 
 
• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements: 
• Fixed Shunt Devices: fixed shunt reactive devices include shunt capacitors and reactors. These devices 
have a fixed nominal rating and their reactive power production or consumption is dependent on

Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability

and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

Background 
 
• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements: 
• Fixed Shunt Devices: fixed shunt reactive devices include shunt capacitors and reactors. These devices 
have a fixed nominal rating and their reactive power production or consumption is dependent on

The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

answer.text:
按NERC资料，动态无功资源在指定电压带宽内随电网电压变化实时连续自动调节无功输出，可维持设定电压或按电压下垂模式运行；静态无功资源在额定电压下输出固定，其能力随电压平方变化，按系统条件投切，投切可为手动或自动，但连通后仅提供固定的额定无功贡献。

仅凭这一调节方式区别不能单独保证匿名厂站故障后电压稳定：该结论还需厂站网络模型、运行点、电压限值与故障/预想事故假设等专项研究，NERC资料只说明资源类型与N-1扰动后应维持在紧急电压限值内的分析框架，未证明任何特定厂站通过电压稳定研究，本次也未做仿真或安全认证。

excerpts.text:
Background 
 
• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements: 
• Fixed Shunt Devices: fixed shunt reactive devices include shunt capacitors and reactors. These devices 
have a fixed nominal rating and their reactive power production or consumption is dependent on

range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements: 
• Fixed Shunt Devices: fixed shunt reactive devices include shunt capacitors and reactors. These devices 
have a fixed nominal rating and their reactive power production or consumption is dependent on

actual_question: 按给定NERC资料解释动态无功资源如何调节输出，以及两种运行方式。

initial_answer.text:
按给定NERC资料，动态无功资源随电网电压变化，在指定电压带宽内连续自动实时调节无功出力，用以维持设定电压，或按电压下垂模式运行；其前提是具备相应的连续调节范围。

两种运行方式即：维持整定电压（定电压）与电压下垂模式。

按给定NERC资料，动态无功资源随电网电压变化，在指定电压带宽内连续自动实时调节无功出力，用以维持设定电压，或按电压下垂模式运行；其前提是具备相应的连续调节范围。

两种运行方式即：维持整定电压（定电压）与电压下垂模式。

findings.rationale: The NERC guideline body states dynamic reactive resources adjust reactive power output automatically in real time in response to grid voltage changes.

excerpts.text:
Background 
 
• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements: 
• Fixed Shunt Devices: fixed shunt reactive devices include shunt capacitors and reactors. These devices 
have a fixed nominal rating and their reactive power production or consumption is dependent on

nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected.

actual_question: 按给定NERC资料解释动态无功资源如何调节输出，以及两种运行方式。

initial_answer.text:
按给定NERC资料，动态无功资源随电网电压变化，在指定电压带宽内连续自动实时调节无功出力，用以维持设定电压，或按电压下垂模式运行；其前提是具备相应的连续调节范围。

两种运行方式即：维持整定电压（定电压）与电压下垂模式。

上述为概念解释，不作厂站安全认证；具体带宽、整定值与下垂参数本资料片段未给出。
assumptions: 仅按给定NERC指南片段解释概念，不涉及具体厂站参数。
missing_information: 给定片段未给出电压带宽、整定电压与下垂率的取值，也未给出具体厂站配置。

answer.text:
按NERC《无功规划》指南，静态无功资源在额定电压下输出固定的无功功率，其能力随电压平方变化，并按其接入点电压变化而增减。

这类装置根据系统条件手动或自动投切，投入后即向电网提供固定的额定无功贡献，而非像动态资源那样在电压带宽内连续调节。

该指南面向北美大容量电力系统，为自愿性建议；具体投切判据和整定值未给出。
missing_information: 具体的投切判据与整定值（如电压门槛、延时）在给定资料中未给出。

excerpts.text:
Background 
 
• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements: 
• Fixed Shunt Devices: fixed shunt reactive devices include shunt capacitors and reactors. These devices 
have a fixed nominal rating and their reactive power production or consumption is dependent on

actual_question: 按给定NERC资料解释静态无功资源在额定电压下的输出及其电压依赖，并说明如何投切。

initial_answer.text:
按NERC《无功规划》指南，静态无功资源在额定电压下输出固定的无功功率，其能力随电压平方变化，并按其接入点电压变化而增减。

这类装置根据系统条件手动或自动投切，投入后即向电网提供固定的额定无功贡献，而非像动态资源那样在电压带宽内连续调节。

该指南面向北美大容量电力系统，为自愿性建议；具体投切判据和整定值未给出。

Background 
 
• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements: 
• Fixed Shunt Devices: fixed shunt reactive devices include shunt capacitors and reactors. These devices 
have a fixed nominal rating and their reactive power production or consumption is dependent on

actual_question: 按给定NERC资料解释静态无功资源在额定电压下的输出及其电压依赖，并说明如何投切。

initial_answer.text:
按NERC《无功规划》指南，静态无功资源在额定电压下输出固定的无功功率，其能力随电压平方变化，并按其接入点电压变化而增减。

这类装置根据系统条件手动或自动投切，投入后即向电网提供固定的额定无功贡献，而非像动态资源那样在电压带宽内连续调节。

该指南面向北美大容量电力系统，为自愿性建议；具体投切判据和整定值未给出。
missing_information: 具体的投切判据与整定值（如电压门槛、延时）在给定资料中未给出。

excerpts.text:
Background 
 
• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements: 
• Fixed Shunt Devices: fixed shunt reactive devices include shunt capacitors and reactors. These devices 
have a fixed nominal rating and their reactive power production or consumption is dependent on

conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected.

Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

actual_question: 按给定NERC资料解释静态无功资源的电压依赖；这些资料能否给出某匿名厂站所需补偿容量？

initial_answer.text:
按NERC指南，静态无功资源（如并联电容器、电抗器）在额定电压下输出固定无功，其容量随电压平方变化，按系统条件手动或自动投切，投入后提供固定标称无功贡献；这是准则性描述，并非对具体装置的保证。

不能。给定资料只给出电压依赖关系和规划中的N-1/N-2校验原则，没有匿名厂站的接线、负荷、运行电压与限额等工程记录，无法计算所需补偿容量。

excerpts.text:
Background 
 
• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements: 
• Fixed Shunt Devices: fixed shunt reactive devices include shunt capacitors and reactors. These devices 
have a fixed nominal rating and their reactive power production or consumption is dependent on

Background 
 
• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected.

Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

Background 
 
• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements: 
• Fixed Shunt Devices: fixed shunt reactive devices include shunt capacitors and reactors. These devices 
have a fixed nominal rating and their reactive power production or consumption is dependent on

excerpts.text:
Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

applicability_conditions: 适用于北美大电力系统；自愿性指南；N-1/N-2为规划运行条件。

Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

Background 
 
• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements:

Background 
 
• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements: 
• Fixed Shunt Devices: fixed shunt reactive devices include shunt capacitors and reactors. These devices 
have a fixed nominal rating and their reactive power production or consumption is dependent on

Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

actual_question: 按给定NERC资料比较动态与静态无功资源的调节方式，并说明这一区别能否单独保证某厂站在故障后电压稳定。

initial_answer.text:
按NERC资料，动态无功资源在指定电压带宽内随电网电压变化自动、连续调节无功，按设定电压或电压下垂模式运行，部分电力电子型可在电周期内响应（如STATCOM约50 ms）；静态无功资源在额定电压下无功固定，容量随电压平方变化，经手动或自动投切，投入后提供固定额定无功贡献。

这一调节方式区别不能单独保证某厂站在故障后电压稳定：N-1及选定N-2须在无操作员干预下满足暂态与电压限值，需结合全网潮流与故障分析评估。

该资料为北美电网自愿性指南，未提供该匿名厂站的运行点、故障集与网络模型，因此不能据此作厂站认证。
missing_information: 该厂站的无功配置、运行点及故障/N-1、N-2场景，用于判断故障后电压稳定。

Background 
 
• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements: 
• Fixed Shunt Devices: fixed shunt reactive devices include shunt capacitors and reactors. These devices 
have a fixed nominal rating and their reactive power production or consumption is dependent on

range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected.

excerpts.text:
Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

applicability_conditions: 适用于北美大电力系统NERC指南的规划运行条件。
N-2为选定情形，非全部。

range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected.

Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

actual_question: 按给定NERC资料比较动态与静态无功资源的调节方式，并说明这一区别能否单独保证某厂站在故障后电压稳定。

initial_answer.text:
按NERC资料，动态无功资源在指定电压带宽内随电网电压变化自动、连续调节无功，按设定电压或电压下垂模式运行，部分电力电子型可在电周期内响应（如STATCOM约50 ms）；静态无功资源在额定电压下无功固定，容量随电压平方变化，经手动或自动投切，投入后提供固定额定无功贡献。

这一调节方式区别不能单独保证某厂站在故障后电压稳定：N-1及选定N-2须在无操作员干预下满足暂态与电压限值，需结合全网潮流与故障分析评估。

该资料为北美电网自愿性指南，未提供该匿名厂站的运行点、故障集与网络模型，因此不能据此作厂站认证。
missing_information: 该厂站的无功配置、运行点及故障/N-1、N-2场景，用于判断故障后电压稳定。
